sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 announcement, August 28, 2025
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. Original announcement explicitly says Code Fast 1 was built from scratch with a brand-new architecture, followed by programming-rich pretraining and coding-task post-training. No total or active count is given. It identifies sonic preview checkpoints and a multimodal variant still in training; neither establishes unchanged lineage to another sized Grok model.

sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 Model Card, August 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened through original PDF web retrieval and independently read complete six-page October 27 HTTP-200 cache /tmp/remaining-parameter-primary-cache/34.txt. Introduction gives coding-focused pretraining and subsequent demonstrations/tool-use post-training. Tables 1–3 report safety performance, not total or activated parameters. Same conversational paradigm, evaluation approach and safety filters as Grok 4 do not establish a shared sized base.

sources.title: Grok Code Out Now, August 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Official Announcements topic by Kody Fisher explicitly identifies grok-code-fast-1 as available and identifies it as the earlier sonic ghost model. This is earlier than the current xAI August 28 announcement dateline.

sources.title: Sonic public preview discussion, August 20, 2025
sources.evidence: Provider admin note confirms public free sonic testing with 256k context. Staff replies on August 20 say it is a partner model, not a Cursor-trained model. The later official Cursor announcement and xAI announcement establish its Grok Code Fast 1 identity. Community speculation about another Cursor MoE kernel project is not model evidence.

sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 public preview in Copilot, August 26, 2025

sources.title: xAI Grok Code Fast 1 historical specifications
sources.evidence: Exact original model documentation specifies 256000 prompt-plus-response tokens, text-only input/output, function calling and reasoning. It explicitly excludes images, audio, video and document files. Provider retirement dates are distinct from xAI API redirects.

sources.title: Grok Code Fast 1 in Microsoft Foundry
sources.evidence: Exact model catalog corroborates text input/output, 256k context and function calling. Description repeats new architecture without specifying topology or parameter count. Provider output limit is not confused with full context.

sources.title: Current native slug resolves to Grok Build 0.1

sources.title: May 15, 2026 retirement and code-model redirect

sources.label: Cursor identifies sonic as Grok Code Fast 1

patch.notes: August 20, 2025 is the earliest documented sonic preview, later identified as Grok Code Fast 1; named Cursor/Copilot rollout followed August 26 and xAI announcement August 28. Preview checkpoints changed. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed after the October 27 review. xAI says this model was built from scratch with a new architecture; Grok-1’s 314B and activation fraction do not transfer. Original text-only 256000-token specifications are preserved. Current original-slug routing to Grok Build 0.1 describes a replacement.

summary: Preserved the twelve non-parameter assessments and freshly rechecked both counts on October 27. Retained explicit null/undisclosed total and active parameters after reopening the original launch/card, later xAI comparison material and training disclosures, and bounded total, active and named-lineage searches. The launch establishes a new architecture built from scratch; unsupported secondary 314B claims, Grok-1 activation fraction and replacement endpoint routing do not provide count evidence.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Retain parameters_b=null and active_parameters_b=null, both undisclosed, after fresh separate review.

parameter_reaudit.total_assessment: Exact release and six-page original card have no numerical size. December data disclosure names the model but counts training tokens, not model parameters. Later 4.5/4.6/4.7 model cards and June framework do not supply an exact-model count. Fresh secondary 314B lead was traced against the actual Grok-1 original disclosure and unsupported Code Fast reuse was rejected.
parameter_reaudit.active_assessment: Fresh active/activated searches and original later comparison review yielded no numerical Code Fast convention. Original Tables 1–3 concern safety performance; full later-card texts have no Code Fast entry or parameter-size column. No dense=total inference or Grok-1 25% activation transfer is used.
parameter_reaudit.lineage_assessment: Launch explicitly says built from scratch with a brand-new model architecture; the card describes coding-focused pretraining followed by coding/tool-use post-training. Shared conversational paradigm, evaluation practices and safety filters with Grok 4 are not unchanged model lineage. The retirement guide explicitly routes Code Fast requests to Build 0.1; this is replacement behavior. No supported sized unchanged base or successor-to-original count bridge was found.
parameter_reaudit.search_findings: Searches returned original release/card/API request-parameter documentation, provider metadata, and secondary directories. APXML asserts 314B while contradicting itself on Dense versus MoE, without exact-model original support. Artificial Analysis leaves Code Fast count cells blank while showing 314B/78B for Grok-1; this is corroborating metadata only. A later ICLR 2026 workshop comparison at OpenReview b0Z6LV2FZQ surfaced only performance snippets and was not fully retrievable; no count is accepted from that incomplete access.
parameter_reaudit.access_limitations: Agent independently reopened original launch, six-page card, December framework, 4.5/4.6/4.7 PDFs, Grok-1 original release and retirement page through web tools. Same-day parent-fetched complete PDFs/texts 26/27/28/29/31/34 were read/searched independently, with cached byte/status/timestamp manifest. June framework web extraction failed but direct original download succeeded HTTP 200. OpenReview b0Z6LV2FZQ returned a browser verification page and direct HTTP 403; not treated as a complete negative.
parameter_reaudit.remaining_uncertainty: Neither total nor active parameters has a supported exact-model disclosure or original nominal comparison convention in the material checked. This documents bounded fresh review, not proof that no disclosure exists anywhere.
